name: Textosaurus
description: Self-updater ShellExecutes an installer with no hash/signature, and BaseNetworkAccessManager::onSslErrors() calls ignoreSslErrors() unconditionally — a plain self-signed-cert MITM (no CDN compromise) = RCE. [Opus-verified: CONFIRMED-D]
limitations: AI-generated static source analysis. Confirm the affected version, platform, update channel, and cited control flow before relying on this classification.

later_review_audit.description: Textosaurus ignores TLS errors through the updater network manager and ShellExecutes the downloaded Windows installer without a hash/signature.
limitations: Source review is limited to the retained commit and does not establish released-artifact or current-upstream behavior.

original_evidence.text: | Textosaurus | https://github.com/martinrotter/textosaurus | ad410b75d691 / 2023-08-01 | Y | N (manual, user-initiated via Help>Check for updates dialog) | Y | https, but TLS validation is DISABLED in code (see evidence) | N (no manifest signature — plain GitHub Releases JSON) | none (no hash/signature check of downloaded installer before execution) | none — installer file is trusted purely because it came from the GitHub Releases API response, unpinned | `src/libtextosaurus/definitions/definitions.h:43` manifest = `https://api.github.com/repos/martinrotter/textosaurus/releases`; `src/libtextosaurus/common/miscellaneous/systemfactory.cpp:58-104` checkForUpdates()/parseUpdatesFile() take `browser_download_url` straight from JSON; `src/libtextosaurus/common/network-web/basenetworkaccessmanager.cpp:48-58` `onSslErrors()` unconditionally calls `reply->ignoreSslErrors(error)` for **every** request made through `BaseNetworkAccessManager`/`SilentNetworkAccessManager` (used by `Downloader`, which fetches both the release manifest and the installer file); `src/libtextosaurus/saurus/gui/dialogs/formupdate.cpp:123-151` saves downloaded bytes straight to a temp file with **no hash/signature check**; `formupdate.cpp:216-232` on Windows calls `ShellExecute()` directly on the downloaded `.exe` |
